CATEGORIES (pathway.json "categories", in this exact order)
["lookup", "credential", "comms", "ticket", "access", "data", "network", "cloud"]

| Category | Meaning (writers must follow this) | UI label and icon |
|---|---|---|
| lookup | Read-only: graphs, address lists, logs, checks after a change | existing "Lookup" |
| credential | Passwords, keys, MFA (for example a console password reset) | existing "Login" |
| comms | Call, email or post to a person or vendor, including sending a key by email | existing "Email" |
| ticket | Close, mark or mute a ticket or alert | existing |
| access | Roles, admin logins, vendor logins, billing access | existing |
| data | Share, send, copy, restore, save, move, keep or delete data: files, links, snapshots, disks, backups, archives, logs, saved configs | existing |
| network | Firewall rules, VPN tunnels, DNS, TLS certs, VLANs, DHCP, Wi-Fi, switch config, reboots, firmware, turning logging on or off on a network device | existing "Network" |
| cloud (NEW) | Change a cloud server, database, storage size or service: stop, start, resize, grow, scale, fail over, delete a server | label "Cloud", lucide icon `Cloud` |

Borderline calls, decided:
- Deleting disks or snapshots is data.
- Deleting a whole server (hc-db-standby) is cloud.
- Growing a storage vault or a file server disk is cloud.
- Turning off firewall logging is network.
- Posting the guest Wi-Fi password is data.

WHY THIS CARD
- Nimbus makes hundreds of changes a week. Real teams put a change gate on production network and infrastructure changes.
- This one class of plan catches both of Nimbus's errors:

- Access, credential, data, ticket and comms plans stay manual on purpose. For example, "Delete 9 orphaned disks" (safe) and "Delete pd-archive" (risky) are both data plans, so the player must read both.

COVERAGE (designed)
